next_steps: Share Q3 product deck + benchmarks (link in Slack)
Post all-hands survey and collect feedback by 2026-10-07
Follow-up doc on Dedicated pricing changes from Finance

Jordan: run small dedicated-pool latency benchmarks for RTX-7000 by 2026-10-07

summary: Monthly company-wide all-hands. Maya opened with Q3 highlights (growth, product launches), Alex covered infra and performance work, Priya reviewed product roadmap and Optimize improvements, GTM gave a short business update, and People covered hiring and org changes. Q&A included questions about Dedicated pricing, private deployments, and reliability targets.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, welcome to the September all-hands, thanks for joining live or watching the recording. We're gonna go about 75 minutes today, lots to cover. Alex you're up for the infra update?
[00:20] Alex Chen: Yeah, thanks Maya. Quick note first, really proud of the team's work on the continuous batching improvements, we've cut p99 tail by around 18% on our hosted tier in production this quarter. There's still some noise in the mid-sequence paths but overall good.
[00:45] Alex Chen: We're also finishing the kernel selector refactor that should make quantized paths more stable across different hardware. There's a small edge case with some smaller sequence lengths where the optimizer picks a less efficient kernel, we have a fix staged.
[01:05] Maya Patel: Nice. Any customer-facing regressions to call out?
[01:10] Alex Chen: A couple of customers saw slight perf variance on mixed workloads when burst policy kicked in - that was misconfigured by our autoscaler, now fixed. We updated docs and will push a short note.
[01:25] Priya Rao: On product: launched the new Evaluate + rollout dashboard mid-quarter, it's already used by about 25% of teams on Redwood Dedicated for canary checks. The Optimize playbooks are showing a median cost reduction of ~22% in early adopters (this is preliminary).
[01:45] Priya Rao: Next quarter priorities: 1) Optimize 2.0 (better quantization suggestions + auto-batching defaults), 2) Console enhancements for token-level cost tracing, 3) Private control plane improvements for on-prem installs.
[02:05] Jordan Blake: Technically, we're prioritizing a couple infra bets: better KV cache lifetime heuristics, tighter GPU packing, and a variant routing policy that considers both latency SLO and unit cost. Expect a staged rollout over October.
[02:30] Samir Kapoor: Research update - we've onboarded two open LLMs for verification, and the eval suite now includes stress tests that simulate long tail token patterns to catch cache thrashing. Also experimenting with 4-bit fine-tuning for domain adapters.
[02:50] Emma Li: Business update - Q3 ARR growth was +17% quarter-over-quarter, bookings slightly ahead of plan, churn's stable. We closed two mid-market accounts on Dedicated deals this month. A note on pricing: we'll be updating the Dedicated renewal model to reflect new GPU classes, Finance + Legal will share details next week.
[03:15] Maya Patel: Quick shoutout to Support for managing a tricky incident last month, appreciate the logs and postmortem. Also, hiring - Hannah?
[03:25] Hannah Ortiz: We're temporarily pausing a couple of non-critical roles, focusing hiring on Engineering infra, Sales for enterprise, and Security. We'll publish a priority list by end of next week.
[03:40] Employee Question (Slack): How do we decide Dedicated vs Hosted for a customer?
[03:45] Emma Li: Good Q - typically it's driven by predictability needs, data controls, and budget. Hosted is fastest for PLG trials; Dedicated for customers needing reserved capacity and SLA. Private is for those with network or compliance requirements. We try to provide migration paths between them.
[04:05] Employee Question (live): Any update on private / on-prem roadmap and audit readiness (SOC 2 etc)?
[04:10] Alex Chen: Private control plane is in alpha with two pilot customers. We've integrated KMS support and are working on audit automation - expected beta in Q4. For SOC2, the compliance team's working on the incoming audit, we'll share artifacts once available. Note: some of the docs' names got munged in an earlier draft (SAML as "Sam el" in one doc, sorry for the transcribe typo), that will be fixed.
[04:45] Maya Patel: We're seeing clear value in our reliability and fallbacks - the smart routing/variant fallback features helped during a cloud region flake last month. That product-level resilience is a competitive differentiation, we should highlight it in the next analyst/partner brief.
[05:05] Alex Chen: On hardware strategy - we're testing an RTX-7000-like instance in a dedicated pool. Early numbers look promising for long-sequence throughput and cost per token when combined with the new quantized kernels. Jordan will run a follow up benchmark.
[05:30] Jordan Blake: We'll also start a teardown of a customer workload pattern to publish internal best practices for batching and cache hints - to reduce people re-implementing naive batching that hurts latency.
[05:50] Priya Rao: Product roadmap note - the API contract for structured responses is getting a minor tweak to better support tool calling and function outputs; it's backwards compatible but please check the migration doc.
[06:10] Maya Patel: On the GTM side, we have three intentions: 1) double down on PLG self-serve funnels, 2) more Dedicated proof-of-values for strategic accounts, 3) partner integrations with hyperscalers for private region support.
[06:30] Emma Li: We'll start running partner-focused webcasts in October. Also, a heads-up: competitive intel shows a couple of vendors pushing hard on price-only play; our messaging should stay focused on predictability, tooling, and total cost of ownership.
[06:50] Employee Question: Is there a hiring freeze?
[06:55] Hannah Ortiz: Not a total freeze - reprioritization. We are pausing non-critical roles and accelerating critical hires. Compensation cycles are unchanged.
[07:10] Maya Patel: Quick leadership update - thanks to everyone, we hit a lot of product milestones this quarter, but a reminder that execution matters more than announcements. Let's keep shipping and keeping customers live.
[07:25] Live Q&A snippets (mixed speakers, occasional crosstalk):
[07:30] Speaker 1: Any update on observability retention costs?
[07:34] Alex Chen: We're adding tiered retention and compression; Console will expose projected bill impacts before you toggle retention windows.
[07:44] Speaker 2: For Private deployments - will we support air-gapped installs?
[07:47] Priya Rao: Yes, air-gapped on-prem is in scope for certain enterprise deals; packaging and install automation is the work item.
[07:58] Speaker 3: How do we communicate Dedicated pricing changes to customers?
[08:02] Emma Li: We'll run a proactive outreach and offer transition credits for a period; details from Finance coming next week.
[08:18] Maya Patel: Okay let's wrap with action items and next steps - Priya finalize Optimize 2.0 timeline, Jordan run RTX benchmark, Emma reconcile ARR numbers with Finance, Hannah publish hiring priorities, and we'll send the deck + recordings.
[08:35] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We value your questions - fill the survey, join office hours, and reach out if anything urgent. Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription has occasional noise, speaker attributions are best-effort. References mentioned: product deck (link in Slack), Dedicated renewal doc (Finance confluence link), benchmark spreadsheet (internal).
